header.stance: 通膨指標轉緩支撐中天期美債，長債表現落後

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 通膨預期降溫，5年期美債領漲

油價再度下跌，家庭通膨預期與基礎價格壓力指標也放緩，週五美債由中天期領漲。5年期殖利率下降3個基點至4.12%，優於下降2個基點至4.07%的2年期，也明顯強於殖利率上升1個基點至4.87%的30年期。科技股急跌增加避險需求，大盤卻接近持平，長債沒有加入漲勢。

10年期實質殖利率與通膨補償各下降1個基點，至2.18%與2.20%，使名目殖利率下降2個基點至4.38%，恢復了部分在週四船運事件後中斷的通膨緩解。油輪持續穿越荷莫茲海峽，帶動布蘭特下跌4.34%至$71.99。Fed政策仍有變數：Neel Kashkari支持今年升息一次，紐約Fed的成長估計則幾乎沒有改變。

信用投資人持續下修本週最大交易的長債價格。截至週五下午，SpaceX $250億發行相對美債的損失約達$3.6億，5年期表現優於20及30年期。其他融資與還款消息同樣具體：奈及利亞動用附擔保的美元交換，約翰尼斯堡在財政壓力下償還債券，Huachen Energy則在漏付票息後再尋求展延。

## 價格指標轉緩，中天期受惠、長債未跟進

全週2、5、10及30年期美債殖利率分別下降12、11、8及3個基點。週五2年與10年期利差維持31個基點，2年與30年期卻擴大3個基點至80。5年期實質殖利率下降1個基點至1.91%，7年期下降2個基點至2.03%，10年期下降1個基點至2.18%；30年期維持2.69%。投資人接受較低的中天期實質報酬，最長端的要求沒有改變。

密西根大學調查中的5至10年通膨預期，由先前3.4%降至3.3%。紐約Fed多變量核心趨勢通膨估計，5月降至3.4%，4月則下修為3.7%，68%機率區間為3.0%至3.9%。排除住宅的服務業，仍是高於趨勢的最大來源，但超額貢獻由0.91降至0.83個百分點；商品與住宅也放緩，改善範圍擴及能源以外。

成長資料卻沒有提供同樣明確的轉鴿理由。紐約Fed即時預測將第2季實質GDP成長估為2.71%，與一週前2.68%差異很小。區間很寬，精確速度仍有不確定性，但中間估計並未顯示急遽減速。Fed會議後受訪的經濟學家，將第4季核心PCE預測提高至3.2%，也上調新增就業估計；政策路徑中位數則認為Fed維持不動至2027年6月。

明尼阿波利斯Fed總裁Kashkari表示，通膨已擴散到足以讓他預測今年升息一次；他是6月會議19位決策者中，預估至少升息一次的9人之一。不過，交易員對快速連續升息的定價下降：年底前升息兩次的機率，從週一近80%降至週五約25%。政策敏感與中天期債券因此受惠，最終利率會到哪裡仍未確定。

季底前國庫券大多走強。4週期息票等值殖利率維持3.68%，6及8週期分別下降2與1個基點，至3.67%及3.73%；13週期下降3個基點至3.75%，17與26週期各下降1個基點，至3.85%及3.93%，52週期下降3個基點至3.93%。7月2日大額交割前，短期現金殖利率沒有普遍上升。

### 週末政策發言與部位觀察

里奇蒙Fed總裁Tom Barkin週日表示，通膨仍太高，但汽油下跌與消費者抗拒漲價，帶來初步緩解。他把AI基礎建設列為一項價格壓力來源，認為溫和限制性的政策合理，因為消費與企業定價仍有韌性。這些發言出現在週五交易結束後，更新的是接下來一週的政策討論。

週末市場評論也指出，Capital Group、Insight、Natixis及Pimco偏好中天期美債，在未來可能升息或降息的不確定性，以及長債較高的通膨敏感度之間取平衡。這種配置可能逐漸擁擠。另有評論關注高融資餘額、影子銀行借款增加，以及槓桿ETF、期貨、IPO與主經紀業務占用銀行資本。波動突然上升，可能先帶來美債避險買盤，再讓支撐槓桿部位的資產負債表承壓。

## 大額發行後，SpaceX長債繼續走弱

一位交易商對SpaceX 2056年券的報價，較發行時美債加175個基點最多擴大28個基點。整筆$250億交易相對美債的損失，由週四稍晚約$3.05億增至週五下午約$3.6億。5年期原本最受買方歡迎，20與30年期則在認購及後續交易中流失最多需求，回吐了承銷過程中的利差收緊；當時訂單高峰曾接近$900億。

較廣泛的科技債融資成本也在提高。美國投資級科技利差截至週四為79個基點，高於5月底74個基點。Alphabet宣布$850億增資後，債券也轉弱。新增股權可以增加債權人的緩衝，但規模同時顯示AI支出及融資需求可能更大。SpaceX股價比債券穩定，股權潛在上檔與長期債務負擔，得到不同評價。

週末估計把2030年前AI與資料中心支出放在$5.5兆，未來5年可能透過投資級市場進行的資料中心融資則達$2.1兆。這些是未來推估，接在美國投資級發行已達$1,750億、創6月紀錄的一週之後，有助理解後續供給規模。

### 還款、展延與控制權

約翰尼斯堡償還ZAR14.4億、約合$8,800萬、票息11.455%的債券，完成ZAR300億國內中期票據計畫的全數贖回。與此同時，財政部長因一項有爭議的ZAR103億薪資協議，威脅扣留ZAR80億中央撥款。未來基礎建設債券將接在如期還款之後發行，但市政府營運及政府間財政關係仍有壓力。

Huachen Energy未支付6月21日票息，計畫再次展延債務，其中包括$6.27億美元券。這家中國電力公司表示，會在30天寬限期內支付利息。2021年法院重整已將同筆美元債延長5年至2026年12月，電價下降與再生能源擴張卻持續壓抑燃煤發電業務。寬限期內付款可避免違約，展延要求仍顯示前次重整尚未解決還款問題。

安大略法院批准Corus債轉股，將使Canso領軍的債權人取得控制權。Quebecor要求廣播監理機關召開公開聽證，認為同業買家更適合長期經營。最終監理核准尚待完成，由債權人控制或出售予策略買家，仍影響回收前景。

Thames Water近£200億重整，可能帶來公共財政負擔。若沒有民間破產融資，特別管理程序估計至少使英國政府支出£33.4億；該公司超過一半的債務與衍生性負債連結通膨。在公部門控制下持續供水，仍會使納稅人在金融債權處理期間，面對未來資金缺口。

信用ETF的波動相對小。LQD持平於$109.50，HYG與JNK各跌約0.06%。一週LQD上漲0.39%，HYG下跌0.23%，JNK下跌0.18%，與個別債券及重整案的明顯變化形成對比。

## 歐洲通膨預期下降，財政問題仍待處理

德國10年期殖利率降至2.85%、創3月10日以來最低。交易員對ECB年底前再升息的定價不到25個基點，兩週前仍反映完整一次升息；存款利率維持2.25%。油價回落後，歐元區2年期通膨交換也從4月逾3%，降至2.2%以下。

ECB消費者調查顯示，早在美伊協議前，5月1年通膨預期已由4.0%降至3.5%；3與5年預期仍偏高，分別為2.9%及2.4%。家庭預估未來一年經濟萎縮1.7%，比4月預期的2.2%稍好，失業率預期卻小升至11.3%。近期通膨恐懼減輕，仍伴隨疲弱成長觀感與較長期價格疑慮。

加拿大第1季一般政府赤字擴大至C$164億、GDP的2.1%，高於一年前1.9%。合併淨債務降至C$5,381億、GDP的16.5%，排除社會安全基金後的債務卻增加4.3%至C$1.49兆。評估當期更大的融資缺口時，須分清社會安全基金資產與其他政府帳戶。

新加坡5月製造業產出年增13.0%，由電子業35.8%及精密工程32.2%領先；總產出經季節調整後，月減0.7%。生物醫療年減24.2%，化學品減11.5%，運輸工程減5.0%。AI與半導體設備仍強，成長分布卻相當集中。

### 紐約收盤後的新消息

Isabel Schnabel週六簡報警告，食品、商品及服務都有物價上行風險，預期仍須升息，才能讓通膨回到2%。她未見工資壓力，也承認和平協議降低了不利風險。這番偏鷹發言，接在週五市場調降升息定價之後，為下一輪通膨資料增加政策背景。

法國國家審計機關在週六報導中指出，政府缺乏可信支出路徑，無法說明如何把去年5.1%的赤字降至2029年3%。這項評估將加入2027年總統大選前，關於發債與財政空間的討論。

英國Andy Burnham崛起後，零售國防債或「戰爭債券」構想再度受到關注。家庭每年投入ISA約£700億，支持者認為具稅務優惠的國防工具可再籌£200億。包括即將卸任首相在內的批評者提醒，這些錢仍然是借款。專門的零售管道可以擴大買方，債務、利息與財政規則的取捨則仍在。

中國在紐約收盤後公布，規模以上工業企業1至5月利潤年增18.8%，5月單月增21.1%。應收帳款增加7.7%，產成品庫存增加8.8%，資產負債率小升至58.2%。獲利改善的同時，更多資金占用在客戶欠款與庫存，負債比率也略高。

## 奈及利亞美元交換取得資金，也帶來追繳風險

奈及利亞在此前數週，從與First Abu Dhabi Bank的$50億總報酬交換中動用約$15億，提供相當於借款133.3%的奈拉證券作擔保。首筆成本為SOFR加395個基點，後續提高至400個基點，資金擬用於再融資高成本債務及支應預算赤字。去年12月底外債為$519億。

這筆融資也使政府面對美元保證金追繳。惠譽警告，本地殖利率提高或奈拉貶值，可能要求追加美元支付，增加外匯壓力；IMF也指出，安排可能限制貨幣與匯率政策。安哥拉與塞內加爾曾採用類似結構。奈及利亞透過傳統發債以外的方式取得現金，本地擔保品與美元義務則被交換條款連在一起。

美國利率對新興市場本幣債的共同影響也在增加。美國與拉丁美洲5年期殖利率的30天相關係數，由2月底0.10升至0.49，墨西哥在6月更超過0.8。土耳其及哥倫比亞同樣對外資敏感。油價降低讓進口國有更多通膨空間，美元走強卻可能使央行不敢立即降息。

塞內加爾提出赤字路徑後，2033年美元債上漲0.5美分至53.73。政府目標從2026年GDP的5.4%，降至2027年4.9%，2029年達到區域3%上限。IMF仍要求由國際民間機構稽核、完成欠款檢視，並加強支出承諾控管。未揭露債務曾使IMF在2024年暫停$18億計畫，公部門債務後來估計為2024年底GDP的132%。新目標提供較好的方向，任何處理方案仍須以確認後的起始債務為基礎。

黎巴嫩違約債交易價格約面額25%，比戰前高點低約5美分，此前2024年9月至2026年3月曾上漲432%。政府自2020年3月對約$310億違約後，未再付款，銀行體系損失估計接近$800億。市場原先期待債權減記可能限制在約70%，仍面對新的戰爭破壞與延誤的銀行重整；主權、央行、商業銀行與存款人之間如何分擔損失，尚未解決。

EMB小跌0.02%至$96.54，DXY下降0.07%至101.36，一週及一個月仍上升0.51%與2.21%。另一項彭博美元指標，6月上漲約2%，全年上漲1.6%。部分民間預測認為，年底前還可能再升5%，或第3季升約2%。這些展望呈現美元借款人的風險方向，並非已發生的債務償付成本變化。

## 科技股轉弱，集中度高的指數承受賣壓

韓國Kospi先下跌5.8%，科技賣壓再傳到美國。費城半導體指數下跌5.29%，Nasdaq 100下跌1.09%，S&P 500卻僅跌0.05%至7,354.02。投資人質疑估值與大型雲端業者支出的回報，也擔憂一項大型AI上市計畫可能延後。大盤跌幅很小，掩蓋了領導這波投資週期的公司更大的價格變化。

MSCI新興市場指數週五下跌2.8%，全週下跌4.4%。新興市場ETF的半導體配置中位數約30%，韓國與台灣合計接近一半；另據MSCI資料，4月底資訊科技占其新興市場指數近37%。這種權重會把晶片股的重新定價，傳到包含不同主權、商品與政策條件國家的投資組合。

即使半導體股下跌，VIX仍下降2.54%至18.41，但比一週前高12.26%。收盤時投資人未提高對整體股市保護的出價，也限制了將美債漲勢解讀為全面成長恐慌的空間。

WTI下跌3.74%至$69.23，一週下跌9.62%；布蘭特下跌4.34%至$71.99，一週跌近10%。油輪持續通行，降低了週四攻擊事件重新造成長期短缺的疑慮。黃金上漲1.20%至$4,078.70，一週與一個月仍下跌3.44%及9.37%。原油再度回落，是更清楚的通膨訊號，也與10年期通膨補償小降一致。

## 接續看勞動資料、歐洲通膨與假日前資金時程

美國數據從6月29日美東10:30達拉斯Fed製造業調查開始；30日接續JOLTS與消費者信心，7月1日公布ADP就業與ISM製造業，2日8:30公布6月非農及初領失業救濟金。招聘、職缺、薪資與工廠價格，將幫助判斷本週實質殖利率下降，是否符合接下來的需求資料。

西班牙CPI初值與ECB辛特拉論壇開幕在6月29日，德國通膨30日公布，歐元區HICP初值7月1日公布。油價及家庭通膨預期下降，已使市場減少升息定價；各國與整體資料將讓ECB更清楚掌握核心服務、食品與能源壓力。

財政部週一標售$920億13週期與$790億26週期國庫券，週二另有$800億6週期，週三有17週期，週四接續4及8週期標售，固定收益市場建議美東14:00提早收盤，7月3日休市。季底供給包含7月2日交割。投標參與及現金殖利率，將顯示市場能否順利支應資金，同時在較短時段消化勞動報告。

overall_summary.headline: 油價下跌、科技債轉弱，5年期美債領漲
overall_summary.session_narrative:
油價再度下跌、通膨指標轉緩，支撐中天期美債。5年期殖利率下降3個基點至4.12%，10年期下降2個基點至4.38%，30年期卻上升1個基點至4.87%。密大長期通膨預期降至3.3%，紐約Fed核心趨勢估計降至3.4%；其成長即時預測幾乎不變，Kashkari仍支持今年升息一次。

科技跌幅遠大於大盤：半導體股下跌5.29%，S&P 500卻接近持平。SpaceX $250億債券相對美債損失約達$3.6億，長天期弱於5年期。奈及利亞則動用$15億附擔保美元交換，在取得資金的同時，也面對可能以美元追繳保證金的風險。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Five-Year Treasuries Lead as Inflation Expectations Ease

Intermediate Treasuries rallied Friday as oil fell again and measures of household inflation expectations and underlying price pressure eased. The five-year yield declined 3 basis points to 4.12%, outperforming both the two-year, down 2 to 4.07%, and the 30-year, up 1 to 4.87%. A sharp technology selloff added demand for protection, but the broad equity market was nearly flat and the long bond did not join the rally.

At 10 years, the real yield and breakeven inflation each fell 1 basis point, to 2.18% and 2.20%, leaving the nominal yield 2 lower at 4.38%. That restored part of the disinflationary support interrupted by Thursday's shipping incident. Continued tanker traffic through Hormuz helped send Brent down 4.34% to $71.99. The Fed debate nevertheless remained open: Neel Kashkari backed an increase this year, and the New York Fed's growth estimate barely changed.

Credit investors were marking down the long maturities of the week's largest deal. Relative losses on SpaceX's $25 billion bond sale reached about $360 million against Treasuries by Friday afternoon, with five-year debt holding up better than 20- and 30-year tranches. New financing and repayment news elsewhere was equally specific: Nigeria drew on a collateralized dollar swap, Johannesburg redeemed a bond despite fiscal pressure, and Huachen Energy sought another extension after missing a coupon.

## Softer Price Measures Support the Belly, Not the Long Bond

The two-, five-, 10- and 30-year Treasury yields ended the week 12, 11, 8 and 3 basis points lower respectively. Friday's move left 2s10s unchanged at 31 basis points but widened 2s30s by 3 to 80. Five-year real yields eased 1 basis point to 1.91%, seven-year yields fell 2 to 2.03%, and the 10-year declined 1 to 2.18%; the 30-year real yield held at 2.69%. Investors accepted slightly less real return through the belly while leaving the far end unchanged.

The University of Michigan survey put five- to 10-year inflation expectations at 3.3%, down from the earlier 3.4% reading. The New York Fed's Multivariate Core Trend estimate fell to 3.4% in May from a downwardly revised 3.7% in April, with a 68% probability band of 3.0%-3.9%. Services excluding housing remained the largest above-trend contributor, but its excess contribution declined to 0.83 percentage point from 0.91. Goods and housing also moderated, extending the improvement beyond energy.

Growth estimates offered less scope for a dovish interpretation. The New York Fed Staff Nowcast put second-quarter real GDP growth at 2.71%, little changed from 2.68% a week earlier. Its wide intervals leave uncertainty around the exact rate, but the central estimate showed no abrupt slowdown. Economists surveyed after the Fed meeting raised their fourth-quarter core PCE forecast to 3.2% and increased job-creation estimates. Their median policy path kept the Fed on hold until June 2027.

Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari said inflation had become broad enough for him to project one increase this year. He was among nine of 19 policymakers who had penciled in at least one hike at the June meeting. Traders nonetheless reduced the probability of a rapid sequence: the chance of two increases by year-end was roughly 25% Friday, down from almost 80% Monday. The change favored policy-sensitive and intermediate maturities without resolving where rates ultimately settle.

Bills were generally firmer approaching quarter-end. The four-week coupon-equivalent yield held at 3.68%, while six- and eight-week yields fell 2 and 1 basis points to 3.67% and 3.73%. The 13-week declined 3 to 3.75%; 17- and 26-week yields eased 1 to 3.85% and 3.93%, and the 52-week fell 3 to 3.93%. There was no common rise in cash yields ahead of the heavy July 2 settlement date.

### Weekend Policy and Positioning

Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said Sunday that inflation remained too high, although falling gasoline and consumers' resistance to higher prices offered tentative relief. He cited AI infrastructure as one source of pressure and viewed a modestly restrictive stance as reasonable, with spending and business pricing still resilient. The remarks updated the coming week's debate after Friday's trading had ended.

Weekend commentary also identified Capital Group, Insight, Natixis and Pimco as favoring intermediate Treasuries, balancing uncertainty about future hikes and cuts against the long bond's inflation sensitivity. That preference may become crowded. Separate market commentary pointed to high margin debt, growing shadow-bank borrowing and the bank capital used by leveraged ETFs, futures, IPOs and prime brokerage. A volatility shock could first draw investors toward Treasuries, then strain balance sheets supporting leveraged positions.

## SpaceX's Long Bonds Lose Ground After the Jumbo Sale

A dealer quoted SpaceX's 2056 bonds as much as 28 basis points wider than their 175-basis-point issue spread. Relative losses on the $25 billion offering grew from roughly $305 million against Treasuries late Thursday to about $360 million by Friday afternoon. Five-year notes had attracted the strongest demand; the 20- and 30-year tranches saw the largest drop-off and subsequent weakness, reversing the tightening achieved during syndication when peak orders had approached $90 billion.

The wider technology sector was also becoming more expensive to fund. US high-grade tech spreads stood at 79 basis points Thursday, up from 74 at the end of May. Alphabet bonds softened after it announced an $85 billion equity sale. New equity adds a cushion for creditors, but the scale also pointed to a larger AI spending and financing requirement. SpaceX shares were steadier than its bonds as investors distinguished those distant debt obligations from equity's potential upside.

Weekend estimates placed AI and data-center spending through 2030 at $5.5 trillion and possible high-grade data-center financing over five years at $2.1 trillion. These are projections, added after a week when US high-grade issuance reached a June record of $175 billion. They help frame the next financing calendar rather than adding to debt already issued.

### Repayment, Extensions and Control

Johannesburg repaid a 1.44 billion rand, or $88 million, bond with an 11.455% coupon, completing redemption of its 30 billion rand domestic medium-term-note program. The payment came as the finance minister threatened to withhold 8 billion rand of state funding over a disputed 10.3 billion rand wage agreement. Planned infrastructure bonds will follow a successful contractual repayment, but the city's operating and intergovernmental finances remain strained.

Huachen Energy missed a June 21 coupon and planned another maturity extension, including for $627 million of dollar notes. The Chinese power producer said it would pay interest within the 30-day grace period. A 2021 court restructuring had already extended the dollar debt by five years to December 2026. Lower electricity prices and renewable expansion continued to pressure its coal-power business. Payment during the grace period would avoid default, while the requested extension showed that the earlier restructuring had not resolved the repayment problem.

An Ontario court approved Corus's debt-for-equity exchange, which would transfer control to creditors led by Canso. Quebecor asked the broadcast regulator for a public hearing, arguing that an industry buyer would be a better long-term owner. Final regulatory approval remained pending, leaving the choice of creditor control or a strategic sale relevant to recovery.

Thames Water's nearly £20 billion restructuring carried a potential public bill. Without private insolvency funding, special administration was estimated to cost the UK government at least £3.34 billion. More than half of the utility's debt and derivative liabilities were inflation-linked. Keeping the service running under public control would leave taxpayers exposed to future funding gaps while the financial claims were worked out.

Listed credit funds moved little: LQD was unchanged at $109.50, and HYG and JNK each fell about 0.06%. Over the week, LQD gained 0.39%, HYG lost 0.23% and JNK 0.18%. Those mild returns sat alongside the more pronounced changes in individual bonds and restructuring prospects.

## European Expectations Ease, With Fiscal Questions Still Ahead

German 10-year yields fell to 2.85%, their lowest since March 10, as traders priced less than a quarter-point of additional ECB tightening by year-end. A full increase had been priced two weeks earlier; the deposit rate remained 2.25%. The euro-area two-year inflation swap moved below 2.2%, down from more than 3% in April, following oil's retreat.

The ECB consumer survey showed one-year inflation expectations falling to 3.5% in May from 4.0%, before the US-Iran agreement. Three- and five-year expectations stayed elevated at 2.9% and 2.4%. Households expected output to contract 1.7% over the next year, less than April's anticipated 2.2% fall, while expected unemployment edged up to 11.3%. Lower near-term inflation fear coexisted with a weak view of growth and persistent longer-term price concern.

Canada's first-quarter general-government deficit widened to C$16.4 billion, or 2.1% of GDP, from 1.9% a year earlier. Consolidated net debt fell to C$538.1 billion and 16.5% of GDP, but excluding social-security funds it rose 4.3% to C$1.49 trillion. The distinction between funded social-security assets and other government accounts matters when assessing the larger current financing shortfall.

Singapore's May manufacturing output increased 13.0% over a year, led by electronics at 35.8% and precision engineering at 32.2%. Total output nevertheless fell 0.7% on a seasonally adjusted monthly basis. Biomedical production declined 24.2% annually, chemicals 11.5% and transport engineering 5.0%. The AI and semiconductor-equipment boom remained strong, but the growth was concentrated.

### Developments After the New York Close

In a Saturday presentation, Isabel Schnabel warned of upside risks across food, goods and services and said further rate increases were expected to return inflation to 2%. She saw no sign of wage pressure and acknowledged that the peace agreement had reduced adverse risks. Her remarks placed a hawkish counterpoint beside Friday's reduction in market pricing ahead of the next inflation releases.

France's state auditor said in a Saturday account that the government lacked a credible spending path to cut its deficit from 5.1% of output last year to 3% by 2029. The assessment adds to the debate over issuance and fiscal room before the 2027 presidential election.

In Britain, Andy Burnham's rise revived proposals for retail defense or “war” bonds. Households put roughly £70 billion into ISAs each year, and supporters argued that a tax-advantaged defense instrument could raise another £20 billion. Critics, including the outgoing prime minister, emphasized that the money would still be borrowing. A dedicated retail channel could add buyers while leaving the debt, interest and fiscal-rule choices intact.

A Chinese release after the close showed large industrial companies' profits up 18.8% over January-May and 21.1% in May alone. Receivables rose 7.7%, finished-goods inventories 8.8%, and the asset-liability ratio edged up to 58.2%. The profit gain came alongside more money tied up in customer payments and stock, and a slightly higher debt ratio.

## Nigeria's Dollar Swap Brings Cash and Margin Risk

Nigeria drew about $1.5 billion during the preceding weeks from a $5 billion total-return swap with First Abu Dhabi Bank, pledging naira securities worth 133.3% of the borrowing. The first tranche costs SOFR plus 395 basis points, rising to 400 thereafter. The money is intended to refinance expensive debt and fund the budget deficit. External debt stood at $51.9 billion at end-December.

The financing also creates exposure to dollar margin calls. Fitch warned that higher domestic yields or a weaker naira could require additional dollar payments, intensifying FX pressure. The IMF identified possible limits on monetary and exchange-rate policy, and Angola and Senegal had used similar structures. Nigeria gained cash outside a conventional bond sale, with local collateral and dollar obligations now linked through the swap.

US rates were becoming a stronger common influence on local EM markets. The 30-day correlation between five-year US and Latin American yields rose to 0.49 from 0.10 at the end of February; Mexico's relationship exceeded 0.8 in June. Turkey and Colombia also remained sensitive to foreign capital. Lower oil gives importers more inflation room, but a strong dollar can make central banks reluctant to use it.

Senegal's 2033 dollar bonds rose half a cent to 53.73 after the government outlined a deficit path from 5.4% of GDP in 2026 to 4.9% in 2027 and the regional 3% ceiling in 2029. The IMF still required an international private-sector audit, completion of an arrears review and stronger spending-commitment controls. Undisclosed liabilities had led it to suspend a $1.8 billion program in 2024; public-sector debt was later estimated at 132% of GDP at end-2024. The new targets improved direction, while the verified starting position remained essential to any settlement.

Lebanon's defaulted bonds traded near 25 cents on the dollar, about five cents below their prewar high, after a 432% rally from September 2024 to March 2026. The state has paid nothing since defaulting on roughly $31 billion in March 2020, and banking losses have been estimated near $80 billion. Expectations of haircuts capped around 70% faced renewed war damage and delayed bank restructuring. Losses still had to be divided among the sovereign, central bank, commercial banks and depositors.

EMB eased 0.02% to $96.54 while DXY slipped 0.07% to 101.36, still up 0.51% over a week and 2.21% over a month. Separately, the Bloomberg dollar gauge had gained about 2% in June and 1.6% for the year. Some private forecasts called for another 5% advance by year-end or about 2% in the third quarter. Those outlooks describe a risk to dollar borrowers, rather than a change already realized in their debt-service costs.

## Technology Weakness Spreads Through Concentrated Benchmarks

South Korea's Kospi fell 5.8% before the technology selloff reached US shares. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 5.29% and the Nasdaq 100 declined 1.09%, while the S&P 500 slipped only 0.05% to 7,354.02. Investors questioned valuations and returns on hyperscaler spending, alongside concern about possible delays to a major AI listing. The broad index's small loss concealed a much larger move in the investment cycle's leading companies.

The MSCI Emerging Markets Index fell 2.8% Friday and 4.4% over the week. The median EM ETF held roughly 30% in semiconductors and almost half in South Korea and Taiwan; separately, information technology accounted for nearly 37% of the MSCI index in late April. Such weightings can carry a chip repricing across portfolios that span countries with very different sovereign and commodity fundamentals.

VIX fell 2.54% to 18.41 despite the semiconductor decline, though it was still 12.26% higher over a week. Investors were not bidding up broad equity protection at the close. That helped limit the interpretation of the Treasury rally as a general growth scare.

WTI fell 3.74% to $69.23, down 9.62% over a week, while Brent lost 4.34% to $71.99 and nearly 10% over the week. Continued tanker traffic reduced concern that Thursday's attack would restore a lasting shortage. Gold rose 1.20% to $4,078.70 but remained down 3.44% weekly and 9.37% monthly. Oil's renewed decline was the clearer inflation signal, alongside the small fall in 10-year breakevens.

## Labor Data, European Inflation and the Holiday Funding Calendar

The Dallas Fed manufacturing survey opens the US sequence June 29 at 10:30 ET. JOLTS and consumer confidence follow June 30, ADP employment and ISM manufacturing July 1, then June payrolls and initial claims July 2 at 8:30. Hiring, vacancies, wages and factory prices will help assess whether the week's lower real yields fit the incoming demand picture.

Spain's flash CPI and the opening of the ECB Forum in Sintra arrive June 29, German inflation June 30 and euro-area flash HICP July 1. After lower oil and household expectations reduced market pricing for another increase, the national and aggregate readings will give the ECB a more current view of core services, food and energy pressure.

Treasury sells $92 billion of 13-week and $79 billion of 26-week bills Monday, then $80 billion of six-week bills Tuesday. Seventeen-week supply follows Wednesday, with four- and eight-week auctions Thursday before the recommended 14:00 ET early close; fixed-income markets are closed July 3. The quarter-end sequence includes July 2 settlement. Auction participation and cash yields will show how readily the market finances it while also absorbing the labor report in a shortened session.
